tips.comment: Not a very original selection but Rising Power should take a lot of beating. He won a very hot looking race first time out at Newmarket. He was eased down at the finish showing a very willing attitude and the horse in third won a very nice race at Newbury today.

The 2yo was a decent 5th of 13 on his debut in a novice stakes at the start of the month, just missing out on being placed. The winner looks like a very smart type. He wasn’t helped with a wide draw that day and a poor track position throughout. That run should set him up nicely for a shot at this £12K selling stakes.

The 3yo is an interesting runner on his handicap debut. He has 1 win from 3. Back from a 9 month break with a nice run three weeks ago. He was only 3rd of 3 in a conditions race, but he made the running and was only outpaced in the final furlong. The winner that day has a 111 rating and finished 5th in the Derby last weekend. So there was some substance to that last race and he might prove to be much better than his opening handicap mark of 86.
Won this last year off an 8lb lower mark. The same top-class amateur rider is on board again. He has a good draw, and everything looks in place for a big run.

The 7-year-old returned from a 6-month break with two AW runs last month. Excuses last time out, but a decent return run, and he seems in good shape. He should be ready for his return to turf and ticks plenty of boxes for this amateur riders’ handicap. Good jockey booking, 7f on g/s will suit him. He ran some decent races in better company last year and is on a very handy mark now going off previous form.

The model I run suggests Lone Star should win this one. Lone Star lines up here with the highest RPR of the 6-horse race. Has an official ranking that's the second lowest, which subsequently means stepping out with the second lowest amount of weight to carry over this 2m 4f trip. Pulled up on last occasion 31 days out and has since had a wind operation. Looks to get back on and improve after the wind operation. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Abingworth should win this one. This result has been driven by Abingworth having the highest RPR of the smaller 4 horse race. Abingworth does have the lowest official ranking, meaning the weight being carried is less than the others in the field. 5 lbs less to the other two horses and 12 lbs less than the top weight. Abingworth comes here with some decent form to go by, a good second place finish only 12 days ago. Race fitness should not be a concern given the recent run. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator predominantly due to the small gap back to second place in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5 pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Max Of Stars should win this one. Max Of Stars lines up here with the highest RPR of the smaller 4-horse race. It does have the lowest official ranking, which means Max Of Stars goes out carrying the lowest amount of initial weight. This does look like a fairly open contest, but Max Of Stars is wheeled out quickly after the good first place only 10 days ago before the official ranking increases by 3. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator due to the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Greenrock Abbey should win this one. Greenrock Abbey lines up here with the second highest RPR of the smaller 5 runner field but has an official ranking leaving him very well treated off this mark. Lowest official ranking by some way, which results in Greenrock Abbey carrying by far the lowest weight over this 2m 3f trip. Sean Bowen, champion jockey, picks up the reins and looks to steer over the line in first. Came 3rd 6 days ago but should get the job done here. Model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model has suggested a long shot for the last race of the day at Newton Abbot. Moro Rock has been predicted by the model as the value bet, and at a huge price of 51s. This result has been driven by Moro Rock having the highest RPR of the 9-horse race. Lines up carrying a comparably low weight to the majority of the other runners, specifically the current top of the market contenders. Moro Rock has 1 stone less than the current market favorite and 1 stone 2 lbs less to the top weight over this 2m 7f trip. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run has predicted National Voice to win this one. Very little data to go by for this one, but National Voice has been picked for this juvenile hurdle. Jack Quinlan picks up the reins for this 2m trip. National Voice goes out carrying the joint lowest amount of weight. No form to go by, all horses running for the first time. 9s offers reasonable value here. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
In what looks like being an open-looking race, I like the look of Higher Kingdom, who has been really consistent by placing in 5 of the last 6 races and has placed over course and distance.
A consistent performer who was unlucky with traffic problems when a beaten favourite last time. This trip suits, and she remains on a workable mark, offering solid each-way value.

Prince does tend to run freely and did too much too soon last time out over a mile at Gowran. Not the most consistent and yet to win in 29 tries, but has placed in similar company. Distance is a question mark for me, but if settling better, could nick a minor spot. Each-way if back to previous form.
Ger Lyons has got a good record in this race, and whilst Colin Keane is in England, Gary Carroll is a good enough replacement. This horse is a real quality animal in this field.
Is two from two at this track and will appreciate the overnight rain, so likely to be able to put in a bold showing here at decent odds.

This horse broke his maiden tag last time out. He found trouble about 2 furlongs out but finished strongly to grab the win. I fancy there is plenty of improvement to come from this horse. With the trainer hitting form and a good jockey booking, I fancy he will win again.

I was just re-watching the last race, wondering why Easy's odds were so high and why they appeared to be drifting. Within that 15 minutes, the odds have come down, so I have now lost the 22-25-1. First up LTO in a higher grade 2 to this grade 3 and ran a lot better than the 6th place result, being only about 1.5 lengths down. Should hopefully be fitter as well today and, in my opinion, has winning chances, not just place chances.
Another chance is given to M Appleby's runner here in Royal Zabeel, who has stuck up Billy Lee to aid its cause.
He needs to improve again but there is reason for hope. One of the improving 3yo's and there may well be an easing in the ground by post-time, which will enhance his chance.
Cowardofthecounty had a tough task when 5th of 6 at Navan, and this race looks easier. He won at Deauville on good ground, so I am hoping he will go well for J P O'Brien, who has 2 in the race.
Two wins in four starts this season. Disappointed last time but has the form in the book to be competitive in what is not the strongest of Group contests.

Unsuited by soft ground on debut and progressed massively to win at this course and distance venue next time out. The handicapper has given Zodiac Bear a potentially lenient mark going into this tough contest. With this choice being by far the least exposed in the field, there is each-way value in this selection for a trainer who does well with his juveniles.

Cracksman filly who is lightly raced and still open to improvement. She won an 18k handicap on her reappearance at Gowran Park (7f) before going down by just two lengths in a listed race at Naas (7f) last month when 3rd/9. With four places on offer, she is taken to make the frame again for trainer Joseph O'Brien, who won this race in 2020.

Has listed class form and is down in grade. Back down to a 1-mile trip and ideal conditions for him today. J P O'Brien doesn't send many of his horses to handicaps unless he's serious about the horse. All the indicators suggest he could do it this evening.
San Aer has been nibbled at all day after showing a little more last time, which should now bring it into this.

Got off the mark on turf after winning twice on the all-weather. Romped the field with the nearest challenger 5 lengths behind. Tends to attract market support, and with in-form claiming jockey taking off 4lb, negating a 9lb penalty, The Real Screamer could progress further in this company.

Making his debut for the in-form Jessica Harrington stable, this previous winner arrives with potential for significant improvement. His last win was impressive and he looks well-handicapped for this race.

Final Voyage is trained by Johnny Murtagh (10 percent strike rate in the last fortnight). 7 wins and 11 places on the all-weather, but was only beaten 4 3/4 lengths last time out at The Curragh, when hampered late on. Each way chance.

MOONLIT MIST is a five year old mare who showed up well when last seen racing in handicap company on the level. The rain around should not inconvenience her previously a winner on yielding ground and a recent spin under the NH code will have helped sharpen her up. Plenty of placed rides for this promising apprentice and with the yard among the recent winners she appeals.

Has had a run over jumps, so has hopefully blown away some cobwebs. He has a decent record at this track with two wins, and this claimer won on him at Navan last year. So, decent each-way chances even if we have lost the price.

Pink Oxalis has been in fine form this year, winning at Dundalk and Gowran Park and finishing second in two other starts. She was only 4th off an 8lbs higher mark back at Gowran last week, but that was in a better race which lacked pace. If she gets a stronger pace here, she looks a good each-way bet with 5 places on offer.
Auburn Avenue has three third-place finishes, including last time out at the Curragh, when keeping over a mile. Extra furlong a positive.
